scenes.title: THAT ZAP IS THOUSANDS OF VOLTS
scenes.say: That doorknob zap is thousands of volts. So why are you fine?

scenes.title: Your shoes steal electrons
scenes.say: Shuffle on carpet and electrons jump onto you. They pile up.

scenes.title: Air gives up at 3,000 volts a millimeter
scenes.say: Air blocks electricity, until about three thousand volts per millimeter. Finger gets close. Zap.

scenes.title: Damp air steals the charge
scenes.say: Damp air steals the charge, so no zap. That's why dry winters are zap season.

scenes.label: BUT THE ZAP LASTS LESS THAN A MILLIONTH OF A SECOND
scenes.src: Air breaks down at ~3 kV per mm (Science Buddies); static discharge lasts ~100s of ns
scenes.say: Three thousand volts, but it lasts under a millionth of a second. Too short to hurt.

scenes.title: WHAT ZAPS YOU MOST?
scenes.say: What zaps you most? Comment doorknob, car door, or switch.
